subject: Boundary hardening: Private runtime data-path & control-plane packet
messages:
From: Alice Hartman <alice.hartman@helios-analytics.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: security@helios-analytics.com
Date: 2027-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Private runtime network isolation + artifacts

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last Wednesday. Our security team is compiling materials for a SIG and CAIQ review for the Private runtime PoC. They asked for a concise packet we can attach to the SIG: a short narrative describing how customer data paths are isolated from Redwood-hosted services, a labeled diagram showing control plane vs data plane boundaries, tenant-to-subnet mapping, representative egress ACLs, and the KMS scope/policy for tenant encryption keys.

Timeline: we'd like to get these items by 2027-09-07 if possible. Can you send what you can share (redacted where needed) or point us to a Drive bundle and the owner for restricted artifacts?

Best,
Alice Hartman
Security Operations
Helios Analytics

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alice Hartman <alice.hartman@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: Private runtime network isolation + artifacts

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline. I've assembled an initial packet and attached the Drive bundle for the PoC. Highlights below and pointers to attachments:

1) Executive narrative (attached: redwood_private_boundary_v1.pdf) 
   - Short summary of separation model: Private runtime uses a customer-dedicated VPC with two primary planes: control plane (Redwood-managed, minimal API control traffic over dedicated peering) and data plane (customer-hosted or customer-controlled subnets where inference traffic and model artifacts reside).
   - Default behavior: no inbound access from hosted tenants to Private VPCs. Outbound egress to public endpoints is restricted by default ACLs; exceptions require documented justification and audit.

2) Diagram (embedded in the PDF)
   - Shows: management bastion (jump host) only inside customer VPC for SSH access, a control-plane egress channel to Redwood control endpoints via a tightly-scoped TLS-only peering, and optional private interconnect options for Dedicated customers.

3) Tenant mapping (attached: tenant-segmentation-mapping-2027.csv)
   - Provides mapping of logical tenant -> subnet CIDR/k8s namespace -> compute-pool label. We redacted tenant IDs in the copy but kept routing/segmentation patterns intact.

4) Representative ACLs (attached: egress-acl-snapshot-20270830.txt)
   - Example policy enforces: (a) allow outbound to Redwood control plane IPs on 443, (b) allow NTP/dns to corporate resolvers, (c) deny all other outbound by default; includes comments about exception workflow.

5) KMS scope and rotation (attached: kms-scope-and-rotation-policy.txt)
   - Customer data keys are tenant-scoped and can be customer-managed keys (CMKs) in the customer's KMS or Redwood-managed but tenant-scoped keys; rotation policy, split-knowledge procedures, and key access roles are called out.

6) Audit sample (attached: admin-audit-sample-202708-redacted.log)
   - Redacted admin actions (account provisioning, policy changes) with timestamps and actor IDs.

Open items we couldn't include in the public bundle: the full control-plane network map (restricted), internal host inventory, and some vendor-specific attestations. We can provide those under an NDA or via your security portal.

Next steps:
- If Helios can confirm which egress destinations need to be whitelisted for the PoC, we can produce a narrowly scoped ACL for your review.
- Jonas is copied for any architecture-level questions and Vivek for KMS/key handling specifics.

Attaching bundle now. Let me know if you want a quick 30-min technical walk-through for your security reviewers this week.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: alice.hartman@helios-analytics.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-31T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Boundary hardening: Private runtime data-path & control-plane packet

Alice / Monica,

A couple of technical clarifications to help Helios annotate the SIG: 

- Control plane traffic: strictly originates from Redwood control hosts and uses mTLS with client certs. The control-plane endpoint is reachable only from customer VPCs over the configured peering; we do not accept inbound control-plane connections from the public internet.

- KV/Cache separation: model KV caches live in tenant-scoped compute and are never reachable from other tenant namespaces; we use network policies + host firewall to enforce (example rules in the CSV comments).

- Egress exception process: exceptions are submitted via the customer console, require justification and an owner, and create a timeboxed allow rule with a tracking tag for audit. Example in egress-acl-snapshot-20270830.txt (lines commented).

If Helios wants, we can add a short appendix that maps each SIG/CAIQ control to the artifact filename (makes their review checklist quicker). Monica, can you add that to the bundle?

Thanks,
Jonas
Staff Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: alice.hartman@helios-analytics.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-01T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Boundary hardening: Private runtime data-path & control-plane packet

Hi Alice,

Forwarding a few KMS and logging clarifications you might need for SIG: we support two modes for tenant encryption keys - customer-provided CMKs (recommended for regulated customers) or Redwood-managed tenant-scoped keys. Key material never leaves the configured KMS/HSM. Rotation is monthly by default for Redwood-managed keys; customers can configure quarterly or on-demand rotation. All key access is logged to the audit stream and retained per the contract (sample attached).

Quick note on audit samples: the attached log is intentionally limited and redacted; our full audit export includes user_id, role, source_ip, and action, and can be delivered under an approved export request.

If you want, schedule a short sync and we can run through the SIG mapping appendix.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference
